questions.question: What is the primary difference between an IDE and a compiler?
options: An IDE is a whole development workspace (editor, debugger, build tools); a compiler translates source code into bytecode or machine code
An IDE runs on mobile devices while a compiler only runs on supercomputers
A compiler is used for writing code, while an IDE is only used for playing games
There is no difference; IDE and compiler are synonyms
questions.hint: Think of the software workspace versus the translation tool.
questions.explanation: An Integrated Development Environment (IDE) provides an editor, debugger, and build integration; a compiler translates high-level source code into executable instructions.

questions.question: Why does a Kotlin/JVM project require a Java Development Kit (JDK)?
options: Because Kotlin cannot compile without an active internet connection
Because Kotlin compiles to standard JVM bytecode, requiring the JVM and class libraries provided by the JDK
To translate Kotlin into JavaScript before execution
The JDK is completely optional and never needed for Kotlin
questions.hint: Consider the relationship between Kotlin bytecode and the Java Virtual Machine.
questions.explanation: Kotlin/JVM programs compile to standard Java bytecode (.class files) and rely on the JVM and runtime libraries bundled within the JDK.

questions.question: What is the standard directory where Kotlin application source code resides in a modern project?
options: src/main/kotlin
app/build/output
bin/classes
root/scripts
questions.hint: Follows the standard Maven and Gradle project directory layout.
questions.explanation: The standard Maven and Gradle convention places production Kotlin source files inside 'src/main/kotlin'.

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between println() and print() in Kotlin?
options: println() moves the cursor to a new line after printing, while print() keeps the cursor on the same line
print() only prints numbers while println() only prints text
println() is deprecated and should not be used
print() automatically creates a pop-up dialog box
questions.hint: 'ln' stands for line, as in moving to the next line.
questions.explanation: println() prints the content followed by a newline character (\n), moving subsequent output to the next line. print() leaves the cursor on the same line.

questions.question: What is the entrypoint function of a standalone Kotlin application?
options: fun start()
fun run()
fun main()
fun execute()
questions.hint: The universal entrypoint name across C, C++, Java, and Kotlin.
questions.explanation: Program execution in Kotlin begins inside the top-level 'fun main()' function.

questions.question: Which tool allows running Kotlin code in a web browser without installing any software locally?
options: Android Studio
Kotlin Playground (play.kotlinlang.org)
IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate
Kotlin Native Compiler
questions.hint: The official online sandbox created by JetBrains.
questions.explanation: The Kotlin Playground (play.kotlinlang.org) is an interactive online sandbox that compiles and executes Kotlin in the cloud with zero local installation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'val' keyword in Kotlin?
options: To declare a read-only, immutable variable
To declare a mutable variable that can be reassigned anywhere
To define a loop structure
To import an external library
questions.hint: 'val' stands for value, meaning constant or read-only.
questions.explanation: 'val' declares a read-only variable whose value cannot be reassigned once initialized.

questions.question: What file extension is used for standard Kotlin source files?
options: .java
.kt
.kot
.class
questions.explanation: Standard Kotlin source code files use the '.kt' extension (or '.kts' for Kotlin scripts).

questions.question: What is the primary cause of the 'No SDK Specified' error in IntelliJ IDEA?
options: The computer's monitor resolution is too low
The project has not been configured with a JDK path for the JVM compiler
The keyboard is not connected
Kotlin is no longer supported by JetBrains
questions.hint: Think about configuring the Java Development Kit in Project Structure.
questions.explanation: 'No SDK Specified' means IntelliJ cannot locate a JDK on the machine. Resolving it involves selecting or downloading a JDK in Project Structure settings.

questions.question: Are semicolons mandatory at the end of statements in idiomatic Kotlin?
options: Yes, every single line must end with a semicolon or it will fail to compile
No, semicolons are optional and generally omitted in Kotlin
Only when printing numbers
Only when running inside Android Studio
questions.hint: Kotlin aims to eliminate unnecessary boilerplate punctuation.
questions.explanation: In Kotlin, semicolons are optional. Developers only use them when placing multiple statements on the same line.
